                                       Resolution 2026-10
                        Of the Girdwood Board of Supervisors

                RESOLUTION OF SUPPORT FOR AMENDMENT OF THE
            PROPOSED 2027 GENERAL GOVERNMENT OPERATING BUDGET
    TO INCREASE AREAWIDE EMS FUNDING FOR THE GIRDWOOD FIRE DEPARTMENT BY
                                               $106,114

   WHEREAS, Girdwood Fire and Rescue (GFR) is the only rescue service or emergency medical services (EMS) in the
    eastern half of the Municipality; and

   WHEREAS, GFR is the sole provider of medical services south of Anchorage for 24 hours a day on weekends and 15
    hours per day on weekdays; and

   WHEREAS, GFR provides Advanced Life Support (ALS) level care with 2 ALS trained providers on shift daily; and

   WHEREAS, the Seward Highway, where Girdwood provides motor vehicle extrication and rescue services had over
    9,000 vehicles per day from May 1- August 31, 2026; and

   WHEREAS, 170,000 visitors have travelled to the Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center, since January 1, 2026 within the
   Girdwood EMS service area; and

   WHEREAS, thousands of visitors recreate, visit or travel within the Chugach National Forest each year within the
   Girdwood EMS service area; and

   WHEREAS, Alyeska Resort is a year-round hotel, spa and mountain resort destination and Girdwood has 391 short term
     rental listings that average a 50% occupancy within the Girdwood EMS service area; and

   WHEREAS, Alyeska Resort documented a 16% increase in summer hotel guests between May-August of 2026 for a total
    of 55,329 guests; and

   WHEREAS, there was estimated in 2026, 36,000 Whittier cruise ship passengers and 140,000 Seward cruise ship
    passengers who transit by rental car, commercial bus and Alaska Railroad train thru the Girdwood EMS service area in
   summer; and

   WHEREAS, emergency medical calls such as cardiac arrest calls, vehicle accidents and recreational traumatic injuries can
    be labor intensive; and

   WHEREAS, funding allocated to GFR for fire protection is funded by a tax levy on property in the Girdwood Valley
    Service Area (GVSA) which, by code, can't be expended outside GVSA. In contrast EMS and rescue are funded from

    Areawide taxes as a service across the Municipality; and

   WHEREAS, 32% of GFR incidents occurring outside of GVSA in 2025, with 62% of incidents in 2026 being EMS calls;
    and

   WHEREAS, Girdwood Board of Supervisors is only able to adjust the GVSA’s contribution to GFR for fire service, and
   GBOS has nearly doubled this contribution from 2021 to 2027, from $793,000 to $1,475,833; and

   WHEREAS, the EMS budget for GFR has remained since FY2024 at $760,288, but GFR projects a need of $879,216 for
    the 2026 EMS budget; and

   WHEREAS, GFR submitted in 2026 rural health and firefighter staffing grants, but have been unsuccessful; and

   WHEREAS, an increase in funding can cover rising costs and pay for staff on a second ambulance for 4 months of tourist
    season;

   THEREFORE, the Girdwood Board of Supervisors supports the proposed $106,114 increase to the 2027 MOA Operating
    Budget allocation to Girdwood EMS.

    Passed and approved by the Girdwood Board of Supervisors by a vote of 5 in favor and 0 opposed on this 21st day of
    September 2026.




    Nick Crews                                              Attest
   Girdwood Fire Department Liaison

    Briefly describe the program’s services.

   Under contract, Girdwood provides emergency medical services, patient rescues and vehicle extrication services from
    Bird Creek to Seward Hwy Mile 75. Includes the Girdwood Valley, Portage Valley and the large tourist attractions of
    Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center and Alyeska Resort.

   Girdwood has 2 MOA Ambulances at the Girdwood Fire Station and medical supplies are provided by Areawide EMS.
   Girdwood has 2 Advanced Life Support (AEMT, EMT3 or Paramedic) level providers on shift daily, one a dedicated
    provider for the first ambulance and the second, a cross trained Fire Captain. In summer 2026, 53% of shifts, had a
    paramedic staffed ALS position. Four senior firefighters are currently in paramedic training with tuition funded by a
    federal grant. All firefighters are provided with EMT1 training (unpaid) within the first year of service.

    Describe the proposed budget increase/decrease.

    $14,600 Provide for increase in nonlabor budget. Nonlabor pays for uniforms, ambulance fuel, continuous emergency
    medical training (EMTB, EMT2, AEMT, Paramedic) and certifications for 41 firefighters. 12 replacement sets of ems
    turn pants are needed. Girdwood has already fully spent their nonlabor budget in 2026 and is attempting to cover 2026
   ems nonlabor shortfalls by generating wildfire deployment revenue this fall.

    $91,514 Provide second ambulance staffing for 4 months (May, June, July, August) and 3% increase for labor costs.

    Describe the impact on the level of services delivered to citizens/customers.
    Second ambulance labor funding will improve emergency response from Bird to Girdwood during May to August 2027.
    Currently when both Girdwood ambulances are transporting patients, Girdwood loses fire protection as the firefighters are
    transporting in the ambulance. Girdwood has applied for federal grants (SAFER act and Rural Health grant) to increase
    department staffing levels. This will also decrease the amount of times, Girdwood requests a station move up from AFD.
    During summer, Girdwood is responding to motor vehicle accidents on the Seward Hwy, increased tourism at Alaska
    Wildlife Conservation Center and Alyeska Resort and cruise ship traffic moving thru the service area from the Seward
    and Whittier cruise ship terminals. Girdwood also takes patients having medical emergencies on Alaska Railroad
    passenger trains headed to Seward and Whittier.
